summary: Michio Kamikawa (1960–2021) specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University (attested 2016).

Michio Yano is an Indologist and historian who studied at Kyoto University and Brown University, training under Kiyoshi Yabuuchi and David Pingree. He lectured at Kyoto University and served as Professor at Kyoto Sangyo University from 1973 to 2015.

Working in Buddhist studies and Indology, Michitoshi Barada studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi. He held posts at Otani University, the Eastern Institute, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Michiya Ito was a graduate student at Tohoku University (attested 1990) and later held posts at Tohoku University (attested 1990, 2001–2004).
Michiyo Hoshi works in Tibetology and linguistics. She held posts at the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa and at Toyo Bunko (attested 2003).
Midori Nishino, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2006) and held a research post there (attested 2010–2015).
Mieko Kajihara specializes in Indology. She studied under Michael Witzel and earned a PhD from Harvard University by 2002.

Migmar Tsering (1956–1999) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, having studied under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche. He served as Head of Sakya College and held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.

Philosopher Mihai Șora (1916–2023) studied at the University of Bucharest under Mircea Eliade, the University of Paris, and CNRS. He worked at the State Publishing House for Literature and Arts from around 1951 to 1969.

Mikaël Bauer specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Kanazawa University and Harvard University under Paul Hoornaert, Noritoshi Aramaki, and Ryuichi Abe, later becoming Associate Professor of Japanese Religions at McGill University.

Mikel Burley specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Essex and University of Bristol under J. M. Bernstein, Jonardon Ganeri, Brian Carr, and John Peacock, and became Associate Professor at the University of Leeds.
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Japanology, Mikio Otsuki held positions as a professor at Hanazono University and as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji (both attested 2007).

Mikisaburo Mori (1909–1986) was a scholar of philosophy and sinology. He studied at Kyoto University and Osaka University, and held posts at Kyoto University, Osaka High School, Osaka University (1950–1973), and Bukkyo University (~1973–1985).
Milman Parry (1902–1935) was a linguist who studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet. He held a post at Harvard University from around 1929 to 1935.

Milo Cleveland Beach is an art historian and Indologist educated at Harvard. He held posts at the Fogg Museum, MFA Boston, Williams College, Arthur M. Sackler Gallery, Freer Gallery of Art, and served as Director of the National Museum of Asian Art.

Milton Singer (1912–1994) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Texas at Austin and the University of Chicago, where he subsequently held a faculty post from around 1941 to 1979.

Min Lin specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. Lin completed postgraduate studies at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005–2006) and became a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Min Ling Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Min Thu Wun (1909–2004) was a scholar in linguistics who studied at the University of Rangoon under Pe Maung Tin (~1927–1935) and at the University of Oxford (~1936–1939).
Minakshi Banerjee specializes in Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Debarchana Sarkar and held a James Prinsep Research Fellowship at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
